name: Wi-Fi name, BSSID and signal strength
plain: Sites cannot read your Wi-Fi network name, router ID or signal bars.
meaning: Wi-Fi identity is a location tracker (BSSID databases map to street addresses). Browsers expose none of it. Proxies: Network Information type on Android, server-side IP geolocation, and the Geolocation API which uses Wi-Fi servers behind its prompt.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: navigator.connection.type
fields.range: wifi or cellular, Chromium Android only

fields.name: proxy: Geolocation API
fields.range: uses nearby Wi-Fi inside the OS and returns lat/long only after a prompt, accuracy 10 to 100 m

fields.name: proxy: WebRTC ICE candidates
fields.range: local IPs hidden behind mDNS .local names since Chrome 75 and Firefox 78

limits.headline: Can't see your Wi-Fi name, router ID, or signal bars
limits.user_action: Nothing. Pages have no way to ask for this
can: See if you are on Wi-Fi or cellular in Chrome on Android
Guess your area from your IP address
Use your location only after you allow it in the browser

story.what_it_is: Sites cannot read your Wi-Fi name, router ID or signal bars.
story.for_you: A site does not know which Wi-Fi you use. That matters since Wi-Fi names and router IDs can pin down your home or workplace. Only your internet address and connection type are visible.
story.for_makers: Router IDs can be matched in databases to street addresses, so they are location data. Browsers keep them hidden. Sites use IP address lookups and a rough connection type.

use_cases.example: An ad network wanted your Wi-Fi name to place you in a venue and uses IP location.
A store wanted to know when you are in the shop and cannot from a web page.
A game site wanted Wi-Fi strength for matchmaking and runs a speed test instead.
A video call tool wanted signal strength and measures packet loss instead.
A fraud team wanted to match known networks and uses IP reputation.
A hotel site wanted to detect that you are on its Wi-Fi and uses a login page.
A company portal wanted to allow only office Wi-Fi and uses VPN or sign-in.

risks: IP address still shows rough place

technical_bounds: Wi-Fi BSSID to location lookup enables physical tracking

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Wi-Fi geolocation of a person's home or workplace
